# `min-properties-decreased`

minProperties decreased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `min-properties-decreased` (both directions), `min-properties-decreased-in-request`, `min-properties-decreased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`minProperties` decreased.

## Why this default

In requests: more objects are valid. In responses: clients may receive smaller objects than they expect.

## Example

From test case [`min-properties-decreased`](../../test/cases/min-properties-decreased/): minProperties lowered on a response object.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-       minProperties: 2
+       minProperties: 1
```

Findings:

- `min-properties-decreased-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  min-properties-decreased: warn
```

## How to fix

Check that clients handle the smaller objects.
